correctness.rationale: PASS: On p1=0 the quadratic p2 is nondegenerate and p4 is not identically zero, giving regular-sequence complete intersection degree 8 of dimension n−4. The singular Jacobian condition makes all coordinates roots of x³=Ax+B, hence 2 or 3 values. Two nonzero distinct values contradict p1=p2=0; for three the identity a(b-c)^2+b(c-a)^2+c(a-b)^2≥0 forces equal multiplicities a=b=c, and the roots are a scalar multiple of 1,ω,ω². Projective equivalence quotients the multinomial assignments by the free cyclic scalar action (factor 3). On W={sum v=sum x_i v_i=0}, the constrained quartic Hessian has radical exactly radial Cx, so on projective tangent its rank is n−3 and all singular points are ordinary nodes. Independent integer calculations confirmed node counts [30,560,11550,252252] at n=6,9,12,15, but the complex n-uniform result comes from the proof, not modular sampling.
